questions.stem: When the quantity of a good demanded in the market is less than the quantity of the good supplied there will be
explanation_steps: When the quantity supplied ($$ Q_s $$) exceeds the quantity demanded ($$ Q_d $$) at a given price, a surplus or **excess supply** occurs. This typically happens when the market price is above the equilibrium price.

questions.stem: Allocation of resources in a free market economy is mainly done by
explanation_steps: In a **free market economy**, the allocation of resources is determined by **market forces**, which are the interaction of supply and demand without government intervention.

questions.stem: Given that Consumption (C) = $$ 1000 + 0.80 Y_d $$, where $$ Y_d $$ is disposable income, what will be the level of consumption if the disposable personal income is Nakfa 30, 000?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify the formula.**
$$ C = 1000 + 0.80 Y_d $$

**Step 2: Substitute the given value of disposable income ($$ Y_d $$).**
$$ Y_d = 30,000 $$
$$ C = 1000 + 0.80(30,000) $$

**Step 3: Calculate the product.**
$$ 0.80 \times 30,000 = 24,000 $$

**Step 4: Final Addition.**
$$ C = 1000 + 24,000 = 25,000 $$

**Result:** The level of consumption is Nakfa 25,000.

questions.stem: The extra satisfaction a consumer derives from a consumption of an additional unit is called___________.
explanation_steps:
**Marginal Utility (MU)** is the additional satisfaction or benefit a consumer gains from consuming one more unit of a good or service. 

**Formula:**
$$ MU = \frac{\Delta TU}{\Delta Q} $$
Where $$ TU $$ is Total Utility and $$ Q $$ is Quantity.

questions.stem: If total assets of a business have decreased by Nakfa 5,000 during a specific period of time and capital has increased by Nakfa 6,000 during the same period, the direction (increase or decrease) of the amount of change in the total liabilities of the business for that period is:
explanation_steps:
The basic accounting equation is: **Assets = Liabilities + Capital**. 

**Step 1:** Express the change in terms of the equation: 
$$ \Delta \text{Assets} = \Delta \text{Liabilities} + \Delta \text{Capital} $$

**Step 2:** Substitute the given values: 
$$ -5,000 = \Delta \text{Liabilities} + 6,000 $$

**Step 3:** Solve for the change in Liabilities: 
$$ \Delta \text{Liabilities} = -5,000 - 6,000 = -11,000 $$

A negative result indicates a **decrease** of Nakfa 11,000.

questions.stem: The adjusting entry to record depreciation of equipment is:

options.A: debit depreciation expense, credit depreciation payable
options.B: debit depreciation payable, credit depreciation expense
options.C: debit depreciation expense, credit accumulated depreciation

explanation_steps: Depreciation is recorded by debiting the **Depreciation Expense** account (to recognize the cost for the period) and crediting **Accumulated Depreciation** (a contra-asset account that tracks the total depreciation taken on the asset).

questions.stem: For a merchandising business, net loss is:

options.C: sales minus cost of goods sold is greater than operating expense
options.D: sales minus cost of goods sold
options.E: sales minus cost of goods sold is less than operating expense

explanation_steps:
Net Income is calculated as: **Gross Profit (Sales - COGS) - Operating Expenses**. 
A **Net Loss** occurs when the Gross Profit is **less than** the Operating Expenses. 
Formula: $$ (\text{Sales} - \text{COGS}) < \text{Operating Expenses} $$.

questions.stem: The safest type of endorsement is:
explanation_steps: A **restrictive endorsement** is the safest because it limits the further negotiation of the check. For example, writing "For Deposit Only" ensures that the check can only be deposited into the specified account and cannot be cashed by anyone else if lost or stolen.

questions.stem:
A firm produced 500 pairs of shoes. The total cost (TC) to produce these shoes is 5000 Nakfa and the total variable cost (TVC) is 3000 Nakfa.

I. Its fixed cost will be __________
II. Its Average total cost is __________
III. Its Average fixed cost will be __________
questions.answer: I. 2000 Nakfa, II. 10 Nakfa, III. 4 Nakfa
accepted_answers: I. 2000 Nakfa, II. 10 Nakfa, III. 4 Nakfa
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Total Fixed Cost (TFC)**
Formula: $$ TC = TFC + TVC $$
$$ 5000 = TFC + 3000 $$
$$ TFC = 5000 - 3000 = 2000 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 2: Calculate Average Total Cost (ATC)**
Formula: $$ ATC = \frac{TC}{Q} $$
$$ ATC = \frac{5000}{500} = 10 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 3: Calculate Average Fixed Cost (AFC)**
Formula: $$ AFC = \frac{TFC}{Q} $$
$$ AFC = \frac{2000}{500} = 4 \text{ Nakfa} $$

questions.stem: The rate at which one currency is exchanged for other currency is
explanation_steps: The **exchange rate** is the price of one national currency in terms of another currency (e.g., 1 USD = 15 ERN).

questions.stem: All of the following are functions of transportation **except**

options.D: helps to communicate with other people

explanation_steps: While transportation physically moves people, facilitating face-to-face interaction, 'communication' as a business function is primarily the domain of telecommunications and media. The core economic functions of transport are moving goods/people, price equalization, and overcoming distance.

questions.stem: In the consumption function, the $$ 45^\circ $$ reference line

options.B: is a line along which consumption expenditure equals disposable income
options.C: is the same as the consumption function
options.D: is the same as the investment function

explanation_steps: The $$ 45^\circ $$ line is a geometric reference where every point on the line represents equality between the horizontal axis (Disposable Income) and the vertical axis (Consumption). Therefore, at any point on this line, **Consumption (C) = Disposable Income ($$ Y_d $$)**.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a difficulty in a barter system?

options.A: absence of double coincidence of wants
options.B: absence of agreement between the buyers and the sellers

explanation_steps: The **Barter System** (exchanging goods for goods) relies on the **double coincidence of wants**, meaning both parties must want exactly what the other is offering. Finding such a match is extremely difficult and inefficient.

questions.stem: A business report which shows the financial position of a business on a particular date is:
explanation_steps: The **Balance Sheet** (also known as the Statement of Financial Position) reports the assets, liabilities, and owner's equity of a business at a specific point in time.

questions.stem: Cash of Nakfa 650 received from a customer on account was recorded as a Nakfa 560 debit to Accounts Receivable and a credit to Cash. The necessary correcting entry is:

options.A: debit Cash, Nakfa 90; credit Accounts Receivable, Nakfa 90
options.B: debit Accounts Receivable, Nakfa 90; credit Cash, Nakfa 90
options.C: debit Cash, Nakfa 650; credit Accounts Receivable, Nakfa 650
options.D: debit Cash, Nakfa 1,210; credit Accounts Receivable, Nakfa 1,210

explanation_steps:
To fix this error:
1. **Reverse the incorrect entry:** The wrong entry was Dr. AR 560, Cr. Cash 560. To reverse it, we need Dr. Cash 560, Cr. AR 560.
2. **Record the correct entry:** The correct entry should have been Dr. Cash 650, Cr. AR 650.
3. **Combine them:** Debit Cash ($$ 560 + 650 = 1,210 $$) and Credit AR ($$ 560 + 650 = 1,210 $$).

questions.stem: The normal balance side of an accumulated depreciation account is on:
explanation_steps: **Accumulated Depreciation** is a **contra-asset** account. Since assets have a normal debit balance, a contra-asset account has the opposite, which is a **credit** balance.

questions.stem:
Use the following employment income tax table:

| Salary range (in Nakfa) | Tax rate |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 – 200 | 2% |
| 201 – 1,200 | 10% |
| 1,201 – 2,500 | 20% |
| 2,501 – 3,500 | 25% |
| Greater than 3,500 | 30% |

Mrs. Hayat earns gross monthly salary of 3,500 Nakfa.

What is the amount of monthly income tax that she will pay?
explanation_steps:
The tax is calculated using a progressive bracket system:

**Step 1:** First 200 Nakfa: $$ 200 \times 0.02 = 4 $$
**Step 2:** Next 1,000 Nakfa (1,200 - 200): $$ 1,000 \times 0.10 = 100 $$
**Step 3:** Next 1,300 Nakfa (2,500 - 1,200): $$ 1,300 \times 0.20 = 260 $$
**Step 4:** Remaining 1,000 Nakfa (3,500 - 2,500): $$ 1,000 \times 0.25 = 250 $$
**Step 5:** Total Tax: $$ 4 + 100 + 260 + 250 = 614 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

questions.stem:
Define the following:
a) Opportunity cost
b) Monopoly Market
c) Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
questions.answer: a) The value of the next best alternative foregone. b) A market structure with a single seller. c) The total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year.
accepted_answers: a) The value of the next best alternative foregone. b) A market structure with a single seller. c) The total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year.
explanation_steps:
**a) Opportunity Cost:** The cost of choosing one alternative over another; specifically, the value of the best thing you give up.
**b) Monopoly Market:** A market situation where there is only one producer/seller for a product that has no close substitutes.
**c) GDP:** The total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor of production?

options.C: goods used to produce other goods or service

explanation_steps: The four main factors of production are **Land** (natural resources), **Labor** (human capital), **Capital** (goods used to produce other goods), and **Entrepreneurship**.

questions.stem: Which of the following product/goods are complementary?
explanation_steps: **Complementary goods** are products used together. A bed and a mattress are typically used together, meaning an increase in demand for beds often leads to an increase in demand for mattresses.

questions.stem: Costs or benefits of an activity that are incurred or enjoyed by a third party who is not directly involved in the activity are called ___________.
explanation_steps:
**Externalities** (or spillover effects) occur when a transaction between a buyer and a seller affects a third party. 
- **Negative Externality:** A factory polluting a river (cost to residents).
- **Positive Externality:** A person getting vaccinated (benefit to the community by reducing disease spread).

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** the function of a central bank?

options.A: managing the monetary system of the country
options.C: accepting deposits and granting loans to the public

explanation_steps: **Accepting deposits and granting loans to the general public** is a function of **Commercial Banks**, not the Central Bank. The Central Bank deals with the government and other commercial banks, not individual citizens.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of general journal?

options.B: It is not convenient for some business firms

explanation_steps: A general journal requires recording every transaction manually in chronological order, which is **time-consuming** for businesses with many transactions. It also does not allow for division of labor (which is an advantage of special journals).

questions.stem: If a customer takes a purchase discount, an entry is made in the ______ journal.
explanation_steps: A **purchase discount** is taken by a business when it pays its suppliers early. Since this involves paying out cash, it is recorded in the **Cash Payment Journal**.

questions.stem: A special journal in which only cash transactions (cash received and paid) are recorded is:
explanation_steps: While many systems use separate Cash Receipts and Cash Payments journals, a combined record for all cash movements is generally referred to as a **Cash Journal** or Cash Book.

questions.stem: If Mrs. Hayat pays 5% pension, in addition to the income tax computed in **question 72**, what is her net pay?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate the pension deduction: 
$$ 5\% \text{ of } 3,500 = 0.05 \times 3,500 = 175 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

**Step 2:** Total deductions = Income Tax + Pension: 
$$ 614 + 175 = 789 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

**Step 3:** Net Pay = Gross Salary - Total Deductions: 
$$ 3,500 - 789 = 2,711 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

questions.stem: List four functions of money?
questions.answer: 1. Medium of exchange, 2. Unit of account, 3. Store of value, 4. Standard of deferred payment
accepted_answers: 1. Medium of exchange, 2. Unit of account, 3. Store of value, 4. Standard of deferred payment
explanation_steps:
1. **Medium of Exchange:** Used to buy and sell goods.
2. **Unit of Account:** A common measure to set prices.
3. **Store of Value:** Can be saved and used in the future.
4. **Standard of Deferred Payment:** Used to settle debts in the future.

questions.stem: All of the following are leakages from the circular flow of income model **except**
explanation_steps: In the circular flow of income, **leakages** (withdrawals) reduce the flow of money (Saving, Tax, Imports). **Injections** increase the flow of money (Investment, Government spending, Exports). Therefore, exports are an injection, not a leakage.

questions.stem: International balance of payment section that summarizes the flow of goods and services between a country and rest of the world is
explanation_steps: The **current account** of the Balance of Payments (BOP) records the export and import of goods and services, as well as investment income and transfers.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** considered an important function of a budget?

options.A: Budget serves as a planning instrument
options.B: Budget serves as a legal instrument
options.C: Budget serves as a control tool
options.D: Budget serves as a social instrument

explanation_steps: A government budget is a multi-purpose document. It is used for **planning** (allocating resources), it is a **legal** document (authorized by parliament), it is a **control** tool (to prevent overspending), and a **social** instrument (for wealth redistribution). Since all A, B, C, and D are functions, 'None of the above' is the correct answer.

questions.stem: A casualty insurance that covers the physical damage for an automobile is called _______
explanation_steps: **Automobile insurance** provides financial protection against physical damage or bodily injury resulting from traffic collisions and against liability that could also arise from incidents in a vehicle.

questions.stem: Semhar Motel makes additional investment of Nakfa 4,000 on January 2, 2018. This transaction will be recorded as:

options.A: Credit to account payable and debit cash
options.B: Debit to cash and a credit to sales
options.C: Credit to Semhar’s capital and a debit investment
options.D: Debit to cash and a credit to Semhar capital

explanation_steps:
When an owner invests cash into a business:
1. **Cash** (Asset) increases -> **Debit Cash**.
2. **Owner's Capital** (Equity) increases -> **Credit Capital**.

questions.stem: Abu Semir Grocery has total sales of 400 Nakfa, cost of goods sold Nakfa 210 and operating expenses are 160 Nakfa; the gross margin will be Nakfa;
explanation_steps:
**Gross Margin (Gross Profit)** is calculated as:
$$ \text{Total Sales} - \text{Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)} $$
$$ 400 - 210 = 190 \text{ Nakfa} $$
Note: Operating expenses are subtracted later to find Net Income, not Gross Margin.

questions.stem: Which of the following are advantages of subsidiary ledger?

options.A: free the general journal from excessive details
options.B: helps locate error in individual accounts
options.C: shows a single account transactions affecting one customer or one creditor

explanation_steps: Subsidiary ledgers (like Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable) provide detailed information for individual customers/creditors, which helps in error detection, organizing the general ledger, and allowing different employees to manage different ledgers.

questions.stem: Which of the following reconciling items requires a journal entry on the books of a company?
explanation_steps: In bank reconciliation, any item that affects the **book balance** (the company's records) requires an adjusting journal entry to update the ledger. This includes errors made by the company, NSF checks from customers, and bank fees.

questions.stem:
The Red Sea Company acquired a delivery truck for Nakfa 12,000 on January 1, 2016. The truck has an estimated salvage (residual) value of Nakfa 500 and an estimated useful life of eight years. The company uses **double declining balance depreciation**. What amount of depreciation should be recorded for years 2016 and 2017?

| Year | Cost Yearly | Depreciation | Accumulated Depreciation | Book Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Date of purchase | | | | 12,000 |
| End of year 2016 | | | | |
| End of year 2017 | | | | |
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate the DDB rate**
Straight-line rate = $$ 1/8 = 12.5\% $$
Double declining rate = $$ 12.5\% \times 2 = 25\% $$

**Step 2: 2016 Depreciation**
Depreciation = $$ \text{Beginning Book Value} \times \text{Rate} $$
$$ 12,000 \times 0.25 = 3,000 \text{ Nakfa} $$
Accumulated Depreciation = 3,000
Book Value = $$ 12,000 - 3,000 = 9,000 $$

**Step 3: 2017 Depreciation**
Depreciation = $$ 9,000 \times 0.25 = 2,250 \text{ Nakfa} $$
Accumulated Depreciation = $$ 3,000 + 2,250 = 5,250 $$
Book Value = $$ 9,000 - 2,250 = 6,750 $$

questions.stem: If a tax system is perceived to be equitable, tax payers might be quite willing to pay taxes without any hesitation. This characteristic of good tax system is referred to:
explanation_steps: **Equity** refers to the fairness of the tax system, ensuring that tax burdens are distributed fairly among citizens based on their ability to pay.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a trade barrier?
explanation_steps: All the listed options (Embargo, Tariff, Quota, and VER) are types of **trade barriers** used by governments to restrict international trade. Therefore, 'None of the above' is the correct choice as they are all barriers.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** a characteristic of a perfectly competitive market?

options.C: Large numbers of sellers and buyers

explanation_steps: In **Perfect Competition**, firms must have **freedom of entry and exit**. This means new firms can enter the market easily if there is profit, and leave if there is loss. **Restricted entry** is a feature of Monopoly or Oligopoly.

questions.stem: The item used as money should not easily decompose and deteriorate. This characteristic of money is ___________
explanation_steps: **Durability** means that money must be able to withstand physical wear and tear and last for a long time without rotting or breaking. This is why materials like gold, silver, or high-quality paper/polymer are used.

questions.stem: The post-closing trial balance involves only;
explanation_steps: A **post-closing trial balance** is prepared after temporary accounts (Revenue, Expenses, Drawing) have been closed. Therefore, it only contains **permanent (real) accounts**: Assets, Liabilities, and the ending balance of Capital.

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions for a merchandising business **will not** be recorded in the general journal?
explanation_steps: In a merchandising business, the **purchase of merchandise on account** is a very frequent transaction and is recorded in a special journal called the **Purchase Journal**, not the general journal.

questions.stem: A credit sale of Nakfa 750 is made on January 3, terms 2/10, n/30. A sales return of Nakfa 50 is granted on January 6. The amount received as payment in full on January 13 is:
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate the net amount owed after the return: 
$$ 750 - 50 = 700 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

**Step 2:** Check if the discount applies. The sale was Jan 3, and payment was Jan 13 (exactly 10 days later). The terms '2/10' mean a 2% discount is allowed if paid within 10 days.

**Step 3:** Calculate the discount: 
$$ 700 \times 0.02 = 14 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

**Step 4:** Calculate the final payment: 
$$ 700 - 14 = 686 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

questions.stem: Depreciation is generally caused by ___________.
explanation_steps: Depreciation is the decline in value of a fixed asset. It can be caused by physical wear and tear (**physical deterioration**), the asset becoming outdated due to new technology (**obsolescence**), or the asset no longer being large enough for the business's needs (**inadequacy**).

questions.stem:
Prepare a balance sheet for Zara Mining Company as of December 31, 2017, from the following data:

* Accounts Payable: Nakfa 3,000
* Net Income: Nakfa 11,400
* Cash: Nakfa 4,000
* Drawing: Nakfa 10,200
* Equipment: Nakfa 16,000
* Capital, January 1, 2017: Nakfa 4,000
* Notes Payable: Nakfa 12,000
* Supplies: Nakfa 200
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Ending Capital**
Ending Capital = $$ \text{Beginning Capital} + \text{Net Income} - \text{Drawing} $$
Ending Capital = $$ 4,000 + 11,400 - 10,200 = 5,200 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 2: List Assets**
Cash: 4,000
Equipment: 16,000
Supplies: 200
**Total Assets = 20,200 Nakfa**

**Step 3: List Liabilities & Equity**
Accounts Payable: 3,000
Notes Payable: 12,000
Capital (Ending): 5,200
**Total Liabilities & Equity = 3,000 + 12,000 + 5,200 = 20,200 Nakfa**

questions.stem: Which value of the following transactions is **not** included in the Gross Domestic Product?

options.D: goods produced in the past years

explanation_steps:
GDP excludes:
- **Intermediate goods** (flour used for bread).
- **Non-market activities** (watering own garden).
- **Illegal activities** (smuggling).
- **Second-hand sales** (goods from past years).

questions.stem: When percentage change in quantity of a good demanded is less than the percentage change in its price, its elasticity will be
explanation_steps: Price Elasticity of Demand ($$ E_p $$) is calculated as $$ \frac{\% \Delta Q_d}{\% \Delta P} $$. If the percentage change in quantity is **less** than the percentage change in price, the result is a value **lesser than one**, indicating **inelastic demand**.

questions.stem: The demand curve facing a monopolist is_________.

options.C: downward sloping from left to right
options.D: upward sloping from left to right

explanation_steps: Since a **monopolist** is the only producer in the market, the firm's demand curve is identical to the market demand curve. Market demand curves for normal goods always slope **downward**, meaning the monopolist must lower the price to sell more units.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics of insurance involves the spread of losses incurred by the few over the entire group?
explanation_steps: **Pooling of losses** is the core principle of insurance. It involves spreading the losses of a few individuals over a large group of people, so that the average loss is substituted for the actual loss.

questions.stem: In the eight column worksheet net loss appears on:

options.B: Credit side of the income statement

explanation_steps: In a worksheet, if expenses (Debit) are greater than revenues (Credit), there is a **Net Loss**. To balance the Income Statement columns, the net loss amount is entered in the **Credit side**.

questions.stem: All of the following transactions are recorded in the cash payment journal except
explanation_steps: **Sold of merchandise on account** does not involve cash moving out; it is a credit sale. This transaction is recorded in the **Sales Journal**.

questions.stem: Which of the following errors can be discovered by preparing a trial balance?

options.A: recording of an incorrect amount to a debit and credit proper side of the accounts
options.C: recording of a correct amount to an incorrect account of the same type
options.D: recording of Nakfa 23 payments as Nakfa 32 on the cash account

explanation_steps: A trial balance only detects errors that cause an imbalance between total debits and total credits. If Nakfa 23 is recorded as 32 **only** in the cash account (and correctly as 23 in the other account), the trial balance will not balance. Errors A, B, and C involve equal debits and credits, so the trial balance will still balance despite the error.

questions.stem: A depreciable asset is reported on the balance sheet at ______________.

options.B: original cost less current year depreciation
options.C: original cost adjusted for current market value
options.D: book value adjusted for replacement cost differential

explanation_steps: Fixed assets are reported at their **Book Value**, which is calculated as the **Original Cost** of the asset minus its **Accumulated Depreciation** (the total depreciation taken since the asset was purchased).

questions.stem: Production cost that does **not** varies/change with the level of output is
explanation_steps: **Fixed costs** (e.g., rent, salaries of permanent staff) remain constant regardless of whether the firm produces zero or many units.

questions.stem: A market structure with high degree of interdependence between sellers is
explanation_steps: In an **oligopoly**, there are a few large sellers. Because there are so few, the actions of one firm (like changing price) significantly affect the others, leading to a high degree of **interdependence**.

questions.stem: If the quantity of potatoes sold declines by 20% when its price increases by 5%, then the elasticity of demand for potatoes will be___________.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Use the Price Elasticity of Demand ($$ E_d $$) formula.**
$$ E_d = \frac{\% \text{ change in Quantity Demanded}}{\% \text{ change in Price}} $$

**Step 2: Substitute the given percentages.**
$$ \% \Delta Q = -20\% $$
$$ \% \Delta P = +5\% $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ E_d = \frac{-20}{5} = -4 $$

**Step 4: Take the absolute value.**
$$ | -4 | = 4 $$

questions.stem: The Housing and Commerce Bank of Eritrea is established with the objective of granting loans primarily for ______________

options.B: controlling the money supply in the country
options.C: construction of houses to solve the housing problem

explanation_steps: As the name suggests, the **Housing and Commerce Bank of Eritrea** was primarily established to provide financing and loans for the **construction and purchase of residential and commercial buildings**, helping to address housing shortages.

questions.stem: A Car cleaning service firm began October 1, 2017 with supplies of 4,000 Nakfa. During the month, the firm purchased supplies of 3,940 Nakfa. At the end of October supplies on hand were Nakfa 2,100 and then supply expenses for the month were:
explanation_steps:
To find the supplies expense:

**Step 1:** Calculate total supplies available: 
$$ \text{Beginning Supplies} + \text{Purchases} = 4,000 + 3,940 = 7,940 $$

**Step 2:** Subtract supplies remaining (on hand): 
$$ 7,940 - 2,100 = 5,840 $$

So, the expense is Nakfa 5,840.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a permanent (real) account?
explanation_steps: **Withdrawals (Drawing)** is a temporary account because it is closed to the Capital account at the end of the accounting period. Assets, Liabilities, and Equity (Capital) are permanent.

questions.stem: Which of the following would improve control over cash disbursements?

options.A: All disbursements should be made out of cash receipts.
options.B: The same person should approve the disbursement and sign the cheque
options.C: Each cheque should be supported by a petty cash voucher.
options.D: The same person should not sign the cheques and prepare the bank reconciliation

explanation_steps: Separation of duties is a key internal control. The person who handles the cash (signing cheques) should not be the same person who records or reconciles the cash (bank reconciliation) to prevent fraud.

questions.stem: A site acquired for the purpose of extracting or removing some valuables such as oil, minerals, or timber is known as:
explanation_steps: Assets like oil, minerals, and timber are **natural resources** (also called wasting assets). As they are extracted, their value is reduced through a process called **depletion**.

questions.stem: A business Organization that has limited liability and unlimited life is known as
explanation_steps: A **corporation** is a legal entity separate from its owners. It offers **limited liability** (owners only lose what they invested) and **unlimited life** (the business continues even if owners change or die).

questions.stem: A shoe making firm buys hides worth of Nakfa 200 from a tannery firm and processed the hides into a pair of shoe worth of Nakfa 315. The value added by the shoe making firm is;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Identify the value of the final product (Shoes) = Nakfa 315.
**Step 2:** Identify the cost of intermediate inputs (Hides) = Nakfa 200.
**Step 3:** Calculate Value Added = Final Value - Intermediate Cost.
$$ 315 - 200 = 115 $$.

questions.stem: The behavior of U-shaped cost curves implies:

options.A: Cost rise, reach maximum and then fall.
options.B: Cost fixed and not changing in the long run.
options.C: Cost fall, reach minimum and then rise.

explanation_steps: A **U-shaped curve** (like Average Total Cost) shows that as a firm starts producing, costs per unit initially **decrease** (due to specialization). Eventually, it reaches a **minimum** point (optimum scale). Beyond this point, costs start to **increase** due to the law of diminishing returns.

questions.stem: The main objective of a cooperative is to

options.A: earns more profit for its owners.

explanation_steps: A **Cooperative** is a business owned and operated by a group of individuals for their **mutual benefit**. Unlike corporations that focus on maximizing profit for shareholders, cooperatives focus on providing services or goods to their **members** at lower costs.

questions.stem: The resources owned by the firm is/are;
explanation_steps: **Assets** are defined as economic resources owned or controlled by a business that are expected to provide future benefits.

questions.stem: Samson owner of Sarina Motel withdraw 4,000 Nakfa for personal use. This transaction will be recorded as;

options.A: cash debited, and Samson drawing credited
options.B: cash credited, and Samson drawing debited
options.C: cash debited, and Samson drawing debited
options.D: cash credited, and Samson drawing credited

explanation_steps:
When an owner withdraws cash:
1. **Drawing** (Contra-Equity) increases -> **Debit Drawing**.
2. **Cash** (Asset) decreases -> **Credit Cash**.

questions.stem: Which of the following might cause a depositor to receive a credit memorandum from the bank?

options.D: A note collected by the bank for the depositor

explanation_steps: A **Credit Memorandum** from the bank indicates an **increase** in the depositor's account balance. If the bank collects a note (receivable) on behalf of the customer, it adds that money to the account and issues a credit memo.

questions.stem: Semhar Metal Work writes a check to replenish a petty cash fund of 500 Nakfa when the fund contains receipts of Nakfa 494 and Nakfa 4 in cash. In recording the check, the company should:

options.B: debit cash short and over for Nakfa 2
options.D: debit cash short and over for Nakfa 6

explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Total accounted for = Receipts (494) + Cash on hand (4) = 498 Nakfa.
**Step 2:** The fund should be 500 Nakfa. 
**Step 3:** Difference = 500 - 498 = 2 Nakfa (Shortage).
**Step 4:** To replenish, the company debits expenses for 494 and debits **Cash Short and Over** for 2 to balance the entry against the check amount.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a reason in rising public expenditure?
explanation_steps: All the options (A, B, C, D) are common reasons why government spending (public expenditure) increases over time. Therefore, none of them is 'not' a reason.

questions.stem: Gross National Product minus depreciation of fixed assets is ______________.

options.B: current transfers from rest of the world

explanation_steps:
**Net National Product (NNP)** is obtained by subtracting the value of capital consumption (depreciation) from the Gross National Product (GNP). 
**Formula:** $$ NNP = GNP - Depreciation $$.

questions.stem: Assume that the output of a bed producing firm is 9000 beds, the total variable cost are Nakfa 2000 and the total fixed cost is Nakfa 1000. What is the average total cost of the firm?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Total Cost (TC).**
$$ TC = TFC + TVC $$
$$ TC = 1000 + 2000 = 3000 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 2: Calculate Average Total Cost (ATC).**
$$ ATC = \frac{TC}{Q} $$
$$ ATC = \frac{3000}{9000} = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.33 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Result:** Since 0.33 is not listed in options A, B, C, or D, the answer is E.

questions.stem: A production possibilities curve does not illustrate
explanation_steps: The **Production Possibilities Curve (PPC)** is a physical model showing combinations of goods a country can produce. It illustrates **scarcity** (the limit), **opportunity cost** (the slope), and **attainability** (points inside/on/outside the curve). It does **not** show prices or **monetary exchange**.

questions.stem: Which of the following account can be categorized under temporary or nominal account?
explanation_steps: **Temporary (nominal) accounts** are accounts that are closed at the end of each accounting period. They include all Revenue accounts, Expense accounts, and the Drawing account. **Interest revenue** is a revenue account.

questions.stem: A purchase of merchandise inventory on account is recorded in the
explanation_steps: All purchases of merchandise made on credit (on account) are recorded in the **Purchase Journal**.

questions.stem: In establishing and maintaining a petty cash fund:

options.A: the Petty Cash account is debited only when the fund is first established or subsequently increased in size.
options.B: the Petty Cash account is debited whenever the fund is replenished
options.C: the contents of the fund should at all times be limited to currency, coin, and cheques
options.D: the contents of the fund should at all times be limited to currency, coin, cheques, money orders, deposited cash receipts, petty cash vouchers, and notes receivables from employees.

explanation_steps: The **Petty Cash** ledger account is only touched when the fund is created or its official size is changed. Routine replenishment involves debiting the various **expense** accounts and crediting **Cash**.

questions.stem: The record that provides a cumulative summary of each employee’s gross earnings, deductions and net pay during the year is called:
explanation_steps: The **Employee's Earnings Record** is a separate record for each individual employee that tracks their earnings and deductions throughout the entire year. This is used for tax reporting and tracking benefits.

questions.stem: If coffee and tea are substitute goods, then when demand for tea increases price for coffee will
explanation_steps: Substitute goods move together. If demand for tea increases (perhaps due to a preference shift), and its price rises, consumers will switch to coffee. This increase in demand for coffee will drive the **price of coffee up**.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a component of investment?
explanation_steps: In macroeconomics, **Investment (I)** includes spending on new capital goods: non-residential fixed investment (machinery), residential fixed investment (new buildings), and inventory investment (change in stocks).

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is **correct** regarding indifference curve?

options.A: higher indifference curve represents high level of utility
options.B: indifferent curves do not intersect each other
options.C: indifferent curve bowed towards the origin

explanation_steps:
All the statements describe standard properties of **Indifference Curves**:
- **A:** Higher curves mean more goods, thus more satisfaction (utility).
- **B:** They cannot cross because each curve represents a unique level of utility.
- **C:** They are convex (bowed) to the origin due to the diminishing Marginal Rate of Substitution.
- **D:** They have a negative slope because to get more of one good, the consumer must give up some of the other.

questions.stem: The fundamental choices that a society must make about the use of its resources include___________.

options.A: what goods and services to produce
options.B: how the goods and services are to be produced
options.C: for whom are the goods and services to be produced

explanation_steps:
Due to scarcity, every society faces three **fundamental economic questions**:
1. **What to produce?** (Selection of goods).
2. **How to produce?** (Labor-intensive vs. Capital-intensive).
3. **For whom to produce?** (Distribution of income/output).

questions.stem: The accounting principle that states for an accounting purposes a business entity is considered to be separate and distinct from its owner or owners is known as:
explanation_steps: The **Business Entity Concept** (or Separate Entity Assumption) states that the activities of a business must be kept separate from the personal activities of the owner.

questions.stem: The sales account that normally has a debit balance is
explanation_steps: **Sales** normally has a credit balance. **Sales Discount** and **Sales Returns and Allowances** are 'contra-revenue' accounts, meaning they act opposite to Sales and therefore have a **debit** normal balance.

questions.stem: Mr. Ibrahim’s basic wage rate is Nakfa 20 per hour and his overtime rate is 1.5 his normal rate. Mr. Ibrahim worked 56 hours during the week. Find out his gross pay for the week.
explanation_steps:
Assuming a standard 48-hour work week (common in Eritrea):

**Step 1:** Calculate regular pay: 
$$ 48 \text{ hours} \times 20 \text{ Nakfa/hr} = 960 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

**Step 2:** Calculate overtime hours: 
$$ 56 - 48 = 8 \text{ hours} $$.

**Step 3:** Calculate overtime rate: 
$$ 20 \times 1.5 = 30 \text{ Nakfa/hr} $$.

**Step 4:** Calculate overtime pay: 
$$ 8 \text{ hours} \times 30 \text{ Nakfa/hr} = 240 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

**Step 5:** Total Gross Pay: 
$$ 960 + 240 = 1,200 \text{ Nakfa} $$.

questions.stem: The cost of a fixed asset minus its estimated salvage (scrap) value is:
explanation_steps:
The **Depreciable Cost** is the total amount of the asset's cost that will be depreciated over its useful life. 
Formula: $$ \text{Cost} - \text{Salvage Value} = \text{Depreciable Cost} $$.

exam.subject: Business and Economics

questions.stem:
1. Economics can best be defined as

A. the study of how to reduce inflation and unemployment.
B. a normative science.
C. the study of the use of scarce resources to satisfy unlimited human wants.
D. the study of how a society ought to allocate its unlimited resources.
E. the application of sophisticated mathematical models to address social problems.

options.A: the study of how to reduce inflation and unemployment.
options.C: the study of the use of scarce resources to satisfy unlimited human wants.
options.D: the study of how a society ought to allocate its unlimited resources.
options.E: the application of sophisticated mathematical models to address social problems.

explanation_steps: Economics is fundamentally the study of **scarcity**. It examines how individuals and societies choose to allocate limited resources (land, labor, capital) to satisfy their infinite needs and desires.

questions.stem: If the coefficient of the price elasticity of demand is **5.0**, then a **10 percent** increase in price will result in a __________ percent decrease in the quantity demanded.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify the Formula**
Price Elasticity of Demand ($$ E_d $$) is calculated as:
$$ E_d = \frac{\% \text{ change in quantity demanded}}{\% \text{ change in price}} $$

**Step 2: Plug in the values**
$$ 5.0 = \frac{\% \Delta Q_d}{10\%} $$

**Step 3: Solve for the change in quantity**
$$ \% \Delta Q_d = 5.0 \times 10\% = 50\% $$

**Result:** A 50% decrease in quantity demanded.

questions.stem: The amount of total cost that rises when the firm produces one additional unit is called
explanation_steps:
**Definition:** Marginal Cost ($$ MC $$) is the additional cost incurred by producing one more unit of output.

**Formula:** 
$$ MC = \frac{\Delta TC}{\Delta Q} $$
Where $$ \Delta TC $$ is the change in total cost and $$ \Delta Q $$ is the change in quantity.

questions.stem: Osman's disposable income increases from 2000 Nakfa to 2500 Nakfa. As a result his saving increases from 300 Nakfa to 450 Nakfa. This implies that his marginal propensity to consume is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate the change in disposable income ($$ \Delta Y_d $$).**
$$ \Delta Y_d = 2500 - 2000 = 500 $$

**Step 2: Calculate the change in saving ($$ \Delta S $$).**
$$ \Delta S = 450 - 300 = 150 $$

**Step 3: Find the Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS).**
$$ MPS = \frac{\Delta S}{\Delta Y_d} = \frac{150}{500} = 0.30 $$

**Step 4: Find the Marginal Propensity to Consume (MPC).**
Since $$ MPC + MPS = 1 $$, then:
$$ MPC = 1 - 0.30 = 0.70 $$

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** included as a separate item in the basic accounting equation?
explanation_steps: The basic accounting equation is **Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity (Capital)**. While revenues are part of the expanded accounting equation and ultimately affect capital, they are not listed as a primary separate component in the basic version.

questions.stem: Purchased a computer to be used in the business for $$ 2,500 $$ Nakfa in cash.

options.C: Debit Cash and credit Unearned Revenue.
options.E: Debit Equipment and credit Accounts payable.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify the accounts involved.**
- The business acquired a computer, which is an asset (Equipment).
- The business paid cash, which is also an asset (Cash).

**Step 2: Determine the effect.**
- Equipment increases ($$ + $$).
- Cash decreases ($$ - $$).

**Step 3: Apply Debit/Credit rules.**
- Increase in Asset = Debit.
- Decrease in Asset = Credit.

**Result:** Debit Equipment, Credit Cash.

questions.stem: Checks received from customers on December 31, but not deposited until January 2 are referred to as
explanation_steps: Checks received and recorded by the company but not yet processed or recorded by the bank are called **Deposits in Transit**. Since the bank has not yet added this amount to the statement, it is an adjustment to the bank balance.

questions.stem: The safer way to endorse a check is
explanation_steps: A **restrictive endorsement** (e.g., writing 'For Deposit Only') is the safest because it limits the use of the check to a specific purpose, preventing anyone else from cashing it if it is lost or stolen.

questions.stem:
Suppose the market for orange juice is in equilibrium at a price of 10 Nakfa per glass and a quantity of 420 glasses per month. Now suppose that at a price of 15 Nakfa per glass, quantity demanded falls to 300 glasses per month and quantity supplied increases to 450 glasses per month.

Draw the appropriate demand and supply diagram for this market. Label your diagram properly and neatly.

![Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/business_economics_2018_q81_1.webp)
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Draw a graph with Price ($$ P $$) on the vertical axis and Quantity ($$ Q $$) on the horizontal axis.
**Step 2:** Plot the equilibrium point where $$ P = 10 $$ and $$ Q = 420 $$.
**Step 3:** Draw a downward-sloping Demand curve ($$ D $$) passing through points (300, 15) and (420, 10).
**Step 4:** Draw an upward-sloping Supply curve ($$ S $$) passing through points (420, 10) and (450, 15).
**Step 5:** Label the axes, the curves, and the equilibrium point ($$ E $$).

questions.stem:

| Salary Range (Nakfa) | Income tax (%) |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 - 200 | 2 |
| 201 - 1,200 | 10 |
| 1,201 - 2,500 | 20 |
| 2,501 - 3,500 | 25 |
| Over 3,500 | 30 |

**Employee Data for January 2018:**

| Name | Position | Basic salary | Overtime | Sales commission | Gross salary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

explanation_steps: According to Adam Smith's canons of taxation, a good tax system should be equitable (fair), certain (clear rules), convenient (easy to pay), and economical/simple to administer.

explanation_steps: A **subsidiary ledger** is a group of similar accounts whose combined balances equal the balance of a specific general ledger control account (e.g., individual customer accounts).

explanation_steps: The **General Journal** is the basic journal used to record transactions that do not occur frequently enough to warrant a special journal. questions.stem: Which of the following steps is the **first** in the accounting cycle?
explanation_steps: The accounting cycle begins by **identifying** economic events from source documents (like receipts or invoices). Once identified, they are analyzed, then recorded in the journal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to occur if a market is **not in equilibrium**?

explanation_steps: Bank reconciliation is a critical **internal control** procedure. It helps detect errors, unauthorized transactions, or theft by comparing the company's records with the bank's records.

questions.stem:
8. The real value of money is measured in terms of

A. what it can purchase.
B. its store of value capabilities.
C. gold.
D. the precautionary motive.
E. its printing and minting cost.
explanation_steps: The **real value of money** refers to its **purchasing power**. It is the quantity of goods and services that a unit of money can buy. When prices rise (inflation), the real value of money falls.

questions.stem: Haile produces **100 units** of pens with an average total cost of **50 cents** per pen and an average variable cost of **40 cents** per pen. What is his **total fixed cost** in Nakfa?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Average Fixed Cost (AFC)**
$$ AFC = ATC - AVC $$
$$ AFC = 50 \text{ cents} - 40 \text{ cents} = 10 \text{ cents per pen} $$

**Step 2: Calculate Total Fixed Cost (TFC)**
$$ TFC = AFC \times Q $$
$$ TFC = 10 \text{ cents} \times 100 \text{ units} = 1000 \text{ cents} $$

**Step 3: Convert to Nakfa**
$$ 1000 \text{ cents} = 10 \text{ Nakfa} $$ (since 100 cents = 1 Nakfa).

questions.stem: The three important injections into the circular flow of income and expenditure are

options.A: investment spending, government expenditure and imports.

explanation_steps:
**Injections** are variables in an economy that add to the circular flow of income. These include:
1. **Investment (I):** Spending by firms on capital.
2. **Government Spending (G):** Spending by the state.
3. **Exports (X):** Money coming from abroad for local goods.

explanation_steps: The Balance of Payments (BOP) is a comprehensive record of all economic transactions between the residents of a country and the rest of the world over a specific period.

questions.stem: Keren Shoe Shop had assets of Nakfa 280,000 and liabilities of Nakfa 120,000 at the beginning of the year, and assets of Nakfa 400,000 and liabilities of Nakfa 140,000 at the end of the year. During the year, the owner invested an additional Nakfa 40,000 in the business, and made withdrawals of Nakfa 48,000. What amount of net income, in Nakfa, did the shop earn during the year?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Beginning Capital.**
$$ Cap_{beg} = Assets - Liabilities = 280,000 - 120,000 = 160,000 $$

**Step 2: Calculate Ending Capital.**
$$ Cap_{end} = 400,000 - 140,000 = 260,000 $$

**Step 3: Calculate the change in Capital.**
$$ \Delta Capital = 260,000 - 160,000 = 100,000 $$

**Step 4: Use the formula for Net Income.**
$$ \Delta Capital = Net Income + Investment - Withdrawals $$
$$ 100,000 = NI + 40,000 - 48,000 $$
$$ 100,000 = NI - 8,000 $$
$$ NI = 108,000 $$

*Note: There appears to be a calculation error in the exam options. If the net effect of investment/withdrawals ($-8,000$) was subtracted from the capital change ($100,000 - 8,000$), the result is **92,000**, which is option E.*

explanation_steps: A trial balance created immediately after posting transactions but **before** making end-of-period adjustments is called the **Unadjusted Trial Balance**.

questions.stem:
9. A $$ 650 $$ Nakfa price tag on a pair of shoes is an example of money functioning as a

A. medium of exchange.
B. store of value.
C. standard of deferred payments.
D. unit of account.
E. None of the above.
explanation_steps: Money acts as a **unit of account** (or measure of value) when it is used to set prices and record debts. A price tag allows consumers to compare the relative values of different goods.

questions.stem: Ranking the market structures from **most competitive to least competitive**, we have

options.A: monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition, perfect competition
options.B: monopolistic competition, perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly.
options.C: perfect competition, oligopoly, monopolistic competition, monopoly.
options.D: perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, monopoly.
options.E: monopolistic competition, perfect competition, oligopoly, monopoly.

explanation_steps:
The order of competition from highest to lowest is:
1. **Perfect Competition** (Many small firms, identical products).
2. **Monopolistic Competition** (Many firms, differentiated products).
3. **Oligopoly** (Few large firms).
4. **Monopoly** (One single firm).

questions.stem: When the Gross Domestic Product is calculated, the

options.A: total value of final services is subtracted from the value of final goods.
options.B: total value of intermediate goods and services is measured in a given period.
options.C: sum of the values added at each stage of production is lower than the spending on final goods and services.
options.D: total value of all final goods and services produced locally is measured in a given period.

explanation_steps: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the total market value of all **final** goods and services produced **within a country's borders** in a specific time period (usually a year).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a trade barrier used by countries to restrict the imports of goods?
explanation_steps: Tariffs are taxes imposed on imported goods. They make foreign products more expensive, thereby protecting domestic industries and restricting imports.

questions.stem: Which of the following financial statements displays the revenues and expenses of a company for a period of time?
explanation_steps: The **Income Statement** (also known as the Profit and Loss statement) summarizes the revenues earned and expenses incurred to determine the net income or loss for a specific period.

questions.stem: A sale of merchandise for cash is recorded in the
explanation_steps: Even though it is a 'sale', the fact that **cash** was received means it must be recorded in the **Cash Receipts Journal**. The 'Sales Journal' is only used for sales made on credit (on account).

questions.stem: Which of the following entries will be entered in the General Journal?

options.B: Goods purchased and paid by cash
options.C: Cash investment made by the owner
options.E: Recorded the year end adjustment for depreciation

explanation_steps: Special journals handle high-volume routine transactions (Sales, Purchases, Cash). The **General Journal** is used for non-routine entries, such as **adjusting entries** (like depreciation), closing entries, and correcting entries.

questions.stem: Which of the following would **not** be recorded in the Cash Payments Journal?

options.B: Payment for purchase of merchandise on cash
options.C: Cash paid to purchase office equipment
options.E: The sale of merchandise for cash.

explanation_steps: The **Cash Payments Journal** (Cash Disbursements Journal) is for recording all cash **outflows**. Selling merchandise for cash results in a cash **inflow**, so it belongs in the Cash Receipts Journal.

questions.stem:
10. A financial institution which is responsible for issuing bank notes and currency is the

A. National (central) bank.
B. Commercial bank.
C. Investment bank.
D. Development bank.
E. Housing bank.
explanation_steps: The **Central Bank** (or National Bank) is the sole authority in a country responsible for issuing legal tender (currency) and managing the money supply.

questions.stem: If a firm produces **nothing**, which of the following costs will be **zero**?
explanation_steps: **Variable costs** are expenses that vary directly with the level of production. If production is zero, no raw materials or hourly labor are needed, so variable cost is zero. **Fixed costs**, however, must still be paid even if production is zero.

questions.stem: A tax is progressive if

options.A: the tax rate increases with the increase in income.
options.B: it takes a greater percentage of the taxable income of lower income groups than of higher income groups.
options.C: the tax rate decreases with the increase in income.
options.D: the tax rate remains the same for all income levels.
options.E: people with high income pay a small percentage of their incomes.

explanation_steps: A **progressive tax** is a tax system where the tax rate increases as the taxable amount (income) increases. High-income earners pay a larger percentage of their income in taxes than low-income earners.

questions.stem: The price at which one currency is exchanged with another currency is called the
explanation_steps: The exchange rate is the value of one nation's currency versus the currency of another nation or economic zone. For example, how many Nakfa are needed to buy one US Dollar.

questions.stem:

questions.stem: A listing of the balances in the accounts in order to determine whether debits are equal to credits is a
explanation_steps: A **Trial Balance** is a worksheet that lists the balances of all ledgers into debit and credit columns. Its main purpose is to ensure that the total debits equal total credits, verifying the mathematical accuracy of the double-entry system.

questions.stem: The bank statement has an ending balance of Nakfa 1,700. There are Nakfa 600 of deposits in transit and Nakfa 2,100 of checks outstanding. The adjusted balance per the bank statement in Nakfa is
explanation_steps:

$$ Adjusted Bank Balance = Bank Statement Balance + Deposits in Transit - Outstanding Checks $$

$$ Adjusted Balance = 2,300 - 2,100 = 200 Nakfa $$

questions.stem: A merchandising business that uses special journals records the purchase of merchandise on account in the
explanation_steps: The **Purchases Journal** is a special journal used to record all **purchases of merchandise on account** (credit purchases). If merchandise is bought for cash, it goes to the Cash Payments Journal.

questions.stem: A tax is **progressive** if

options.A: the tax rate increases with the increase in income.
options.B: it takes a greater percentage of the taxable income of lower income groups than of higher income groups.
options.C: the tax rate decreases with the increase in income.
options.D: the tax rate remains the same for all income levels.
options.E: people with high income pay a small percentage of their incomes.

explanation_steps:
Tax systems are categorized by how the rate changes relative to income.

- **Progressive Tax:** Higher income = Higher tax rate (Option A).
- **Regressive Tax:** Lower income groups pay a higher percentage (Option B).
- **Proportional (Flat) Tax:** Same rate for everyone (Option D).
**Result:** Option A.

questions.stem: All are characteristics of central planned economic system **except**,

options.A: economic decision is made by government
options.C: market force of demand and supply has little influence

explanation_steps: In a centrally planned (command) economy, the government makes all major economic decisions and owns most resources. Competition is a key feature of a **market economy**, not a planned one.

questions.stem: Which of the following is advantage of both sole proprietorship & partnership?
explanation_steps: Both sole proprietorships and partnerships are relatively easy and inexpensive to establish and dissolve compared to corporations, which require complex legal procedures.

questions.stem: What will be the price elasticity of supply when price increases from 15 Nakfa to 20 Nakfa?
explanation_steps:
Based on the table provided in Q19:
**Step 1: Identify coordinates**
At $$ P_1 = 15, Q_1 = 150 $$
At $$ P_2 = 20, Q_2 = 200 $$

**Step 2: Calculate % change**
$$ \% \Delta Qs = \frac{200 - 150}{150} = 33.33\% $$
$$ \% \Delta P = \frac{20 - 15}{15} = 33.33\% $$

**Step 3: Calculate Es**
$$ Es = \frac{33.33\%}{33.33\%} = 1 $$ (Unitary Elastic)

questions.stem: Given average total cost is $$ 20 $$, fixed cost $$ 50 $$, and total unit of output is $$ 10 $$. Then, find Average variable cost.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Average Fixed Cost (AFC).**
$$ AFC = \frac{TFC}{Q} = \frac{50}{10} = 5 $$

**Step 2: Use the Average Total Cost (ATC) formula.**
$$ ATC = AFC + AVC $$
$$ 20 = 5 + AVC $$

**Step 3: Solve for AVC.**
$$ AVC = 20 - 5 = 15 $$

questions.stem: Which of the following account cannot be found in the financial statement of Merchandising business?
explanation_steps: A merchandising business earns income by buying and selling physical products, so it uses accounts like **Merchandise Inventory** and **Cost of Goods Sold (COGS)**. **Service Revenue** is specific to service-based businesses (like consultants or law firms) that sell time/expertise rather than physical goods.

questions.stem: Which type of accounts will appear in the post-closing trial balance?

options.C: Accounts shown in the income statement of a work sheet.

explanation_steps: The post-closing trial balance is prepared after the closing entries have been posted. Since temporary accounts (revenues, expenses, and drawings) are closed to zero, only permanent accounts (assets, liabilities, and owner's equity) remain with balances.

questions.stem: Which of the following account is recorded in cash receipt journal?
explanation_steps: A **Sales Discount** is recorded in the Cash Receipts Journal when a customer pays their account within the discount period, as it involves the actual receipt of cash.

questions.stem: ________________ is a cost that varies with the amount of output produced.
explanation_steps: Variable costs are costs that change in direct proportion to the level of production. Examples include raw materials and direct labor.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **not** a service sector in an economy?
explanation_steps: Construction is classified under the **secondary sector** (industrial sector) because it involves building and manufacturing infrastructure. Transportation, communication, education, and healthcare are part of the **tertiary sector** (service sector).

questions.stem: Which function of money is used to save purchasing power from the time an income is received until the time it spent?
explanation_steps: The **store of value** function allows money to be held and exchanged for goods and services in the future, preserving purchasing power over time.

questions.stem: Total revenue rises when price rises, then the demand curve is;
explanation_steps: If demand is **inelastic** ($$ |Ed| < 1 $$), consumers are not very sensitive to price changes. Therefore, an increase in price leads to a proportionately smaller decrease in quantity demanded, causing Total Revenue ($$ P \times Q $$) to increase.

questions.stem: Money owed for goods bought by the business is;
explanation_steps: Money owed to suppliers for goods or services purchased on credit is recorded as **Accounts Payable**. It is a short-term liability for the business.

questions.stem: An entry journalized in order to rectify errors recorded is;
explanation_steps: A **Correcting Entry** is made when an error is discovered in the journal or ledger. Unlike adjusting entries, which are planned, correcting entries are only made when a mistake needs to be fixed.

questions.stem: In the work sheet, net income is entered in the following columns:
explanation_steps: In a 10-column worksheet, if there is a net income (Revenues > Expenses), it is recorded as a balancing figure on the Debit side of the Income Statement columns and on the Credit side of the Balance Sheet columns (representing an increase in equity).

questions.stem: All of the following are recorded in a general journal, **except**
explanation_steps: A **Purchase Discount** is recorded in the Cash Payments (Disbursement) Journal when the business pays a supplier within the discount period. Adjusting, closing, and returns on account are typically handled in the General Journal if special journals for those don't exist.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not included in the current account section of the balance of payments?

options.A: The export of goods and services
options.B: The import of goods and services

explanation_steps: The **Current Account** records the trade of goods and services, and income transfers. **Capital inflows** (investments, loans) are recorded in the **Capital and Financial Account**.

questions.stem: Explain the law of demand?
questions.answer: The law of demand states that, other things being equal (ceteris paribus), as the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded decreases; and as the price decreases, the quantity demanded increases.
accepted_answers: The law of demand states that, other things being equal (ceteris paribus), as the price of a good increases, the quantity demanded decreases; and as the price decreases, the quantity demanded increases.
explanation_steps: The law of demand describes an inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a man-made physical good used to produce other goods or services?
explanation_steps: In economics, a **capital good** is a man-made tool or machine used in the production process. A tractor is a classic example of a capital good used to produce agricultural products. While others are physical goods, they are often treated as consumer durables in this context.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics of good money states that money should be uniform quality and capable of standardization?
explanation_steps: **Homogeneity** means that all units of money (e.g., every 10 Nakfa note) must be identical in terms of quality and appearance to avoid confusion.

questions.stem: Which of the following costs do not change with the amount of output produced?
explanation_steps: **Fixed costs** are expenses that do not change regardless of how much a company produces or sells. Examples include rent, insurance, and salaries of permanent staff.

questions.stem: A list of account title along with their number showing the arrangement of the account in the ledger is called
explanation_steps: A **Chart of Accounts** is an index of all financial accounts in the general ledger of a company, typically arranged by account type (Assets, Liabilities, etc.) and assigned unique numbers.

questions.stem: Which of the following account should be closed to income summary at the end of the year?
explanation_steps: All **temporary accounts** (revenues and expenses) must be closed to the **Income Summary** account at the end of the fiscal year. This includes all items listed (Depreciation expense, Sales, Supply expense, and Rent income).

questions.stem: Which of the following is not part of the recording process?
explanation_steps: The recording process specifically refers to the steps of analyzing, journalizing, and posting. Preparing a trial balance is a summarizing step that occurs after the recording process is complete.

questions.stem: Warsay Yikealo secondary school purchase stationary at an invoice price of Nakfa $$ 5,000 $$ and terms $$ 5/10, n/30 $$. If Warsay Yikealo pays the invoice within the discount period, the amount paid will be:
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate the discount amount.**
$$ \text{Discount} = \text{Invoice Price} \times \text{Discount Rate} $$
$$ \text{Discount} = 5,000 \times 0.05 = 250 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 2: Calculate the net amount paid.**
$$ \text{Amount Paid} = \text{Invoice Price} - \text{Discount} $$
$$ \text{Amount Paid} = 5,000 - 250 = 4,750 \text{ Nakfa} $$

questions.stem: ____________ is the decrease in value of domestic currency relative to foreign currency by the government policy.
explanation_steps: **Devaluation** is a deliberate downward adjustment of the value of a country's currency relative to another currency, group of currencies, or currency standard, implemented by the government.

questions.stem: Define exchange rate?
questions.answer: Exchange rate is the value of one nation's currency in terms of another nation's currency.
accepted_answers: Exchange rate is the value of one nation's currency in terms of another nation's currency.
explanation_steps: It tells you how much of one currency you can buy with another (e.g., 1 USD = 15 Nakfa).

questions.stem: A corporation is a form of an independent legal entity which characterized by
explanation_steps: A corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners. Its primary characteristic is **limited liability**, meaning shareholders are only responsible for the company's debts up to the amount they invested.

questions.stem: All are functions of national bank, **except**
explanation_steps: A National (Central) Bank performs all the listed functions: issuing currency, holding commercial bank reserves, advising the government on fiscal policy, and providing emergency loans to banks (lender of last resort).

questions.stem: From the given **TC = 40 + 10Q**, where TC is total cost and Q is output. What will be the amount of total fixed cost?
explanation_steps: In the linear cost function $$ TC = TFC + TVC(Q) $$, the constant term represents Total Fixed Cost (TFC). In the equation $$ TC = 40 + 10Q $$, the constant is **40**.

questions.stem: Ms. Nawal purchased office equipment for cash; this transaction will be recorded in the general journal as;
explanation_steps: When an asset is purchased for cash, the asset account (Office Equipment) increases (**Debit**) and the cash account decreases (**Credit**).

questions.stem: Each time an entry is recorded in purchase journal, the credit would be entered in,
explanation_steps: The **Purchase Journal** is used specifically to record the purchase of merchandise **on account** (on credit). Therefore, every entry involves an increase in liability, which is a **Credit to Accounts Payable**.

questions.stem: Accumulated depreciation is:
explanation_steps: Accumulated depreciation is a contra asset account. It has a normal credit balance and is subtracted from the related fixed asset on the balance sheet to show the asset's book value.

questions.stem: The sum of the cost of the beginning merchandise inventory and the cost of merchandise purchased during the period including the freight-in is;

options.E: cost of goods available for sale

explanation_steps:
The formula for **Cost of Goods Available for Sale** is: 
$$ \text{Beginning Inventory} + \text{Net Purchases} + \text{Freight-in} $$. 
This represents the total value of all goods a business could have sold during the period.

questions.stem: At the end of the accounting period, if the cash short or over account has a debit balance it’s shown on the income statement as
explanation_steps: A **debit balance** in the 'Cash Short and Over' account indicates that the actual cash is less than what the records show (a shortage). This is treated as a **Miscellaneous Expense** on the income statement.

questions.stem:
Given the linear supply and demand equation, $$ QS = 100 + 100p $$ and $$ QD = 700 – 200p $$; where Qs is quantity supply and Qd is quantity demand.
A. Calculate the equilibrium price and quantity.
B. Draw the graph and show the effect of Increase in demand, in equilibrium price and quantity.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Set QS = QD to find equilibrium.**
$$ 100 + 100p = 700 - 200p $$
$$ 100p + 200p = 700 - 100 $$
$$ 300p = 600 $$
$$ p = 2 $$

**Step 2: Substitute p into either equation to find Q.**
$$ Q = 100 + 100(2) = 100 + 200 = 300 $$

**B. Graphing:**
An increase in demand shifts the demand curve to the right, leading to a higher equilibrium price and a higher equilibrium quantity.

questions.stem: A means of communication system that transmits information through microwave, radio and television is;
explanation_steps: **Telecommunication** involves the transmission of signs, signals, messages, words, writings, images, and sounds by wire, radio, optical, or other electromagnetic systems.

questions.stem: Which type of bank helps poor households to improve their living standards?
explanation_steps: **Micro credit programs** provide small loans to low-income individuals or households who lack access to traditional banking services, helping them start small businesses and improve their livelihood.

questions.stem: An increase in the cost of producing output, cetris paribus,

options.A: Increases the price level and decreases real output,
options.B: Increases the price level and increases real output,
options.C: Increases the level of price has no effect up on real output,
options.D: Decreases the level of price and decreases real output level,
options.E: Real output increase once output is at its full employment level.

explanation_steps: An increase in production costs (e.g., higher wages or raw material prices) causes the **Aggregate Supply (AS)** curve to shift to the left. This results in a higher price level (inflation) and a lower level of real output (recession).

questions.stem: Payment of liability by a business will be recorded as;
explanation_steps: Paying a liability decreases the liability (Debit) and decreases the asset cash (Credit). Therefore, **Account Payable** is debited.

questions.stem: All of the transactions are recorded in the cash receipt journal, **except**
explanation_steps: **Sold of merchandise on account** (credit sale) does not involve cash immediately. It is recorded in the **Sales Journal**. The Cash Receipt Journal only records transactions where cash is actually received.

questions.stem: The order of the account in the ledger is as follows:

options.A: Assets, revenue, expense, liabilities, owners’ capital & owners’ equity
options.B: Assets, liabilities, owners’ capital, owners drawing, revenue & expense
options.C: Owners capital, assets, revenues, expense, liabilities & owners drawing
options.D: Revenue, assets, expense, liabilities, owners’ capital & owners drawing

explanation_steps: Accounts in the general ledger are typically arranged in the order they appear in the financial statements: Assets, Liabilities, Owner's Equity (Capital then Drawing), Revenues, and Expenses.

questions.stem: Which of the following accounts is closed to debit side?
explanation_steps: **Sales** has a normal credit balance. To close it at the end of the period, you must **Debit Sales** and Credit Income Summary. All other options (Purchases, Expenses, Freight) have normal debit balances and are closed with a credit.

questions.stem: The amount of money to be given to employees before any obligation or loan is deducted is referred to as:
explanation_steps: **Gross Pay** is the total earnings of an employee (salary, wages, overtime) before any taxes, insurance, or other deductions are taken out.

questions.stem: List four factors that affect price elasticity of demand?
questions.answer: 1. Availability of substitutes, 2. Proportion of income spent on the good, 3. Nature of the good (Necessity vs. Luxury), 4. Time period.
accepted_answers: 1. Availability of substitutes, 2. Proportion of income spent on the good, 3. Nature of the good (Necessity vs. Luxury), 4. Time period.
explanation_steps: These factors determine how sensitive consumers are to price changes. For example, goods with many substitutes are more elastic.

questions.stem: All are characteristics of corporate form of business organization, **except**
explanation_steps: Corporations usually have the advantage of raising **large amounts of capital** by selling shares to the public. Therefore, 'Limited capital' is not a characteristic; rather, they have access to vast capital.

questions.stem: Insurance principle that states individuals should not claim compensation from two sources is;
explanation_steps: The principle of **Contribution** states that if an insured has taken multiple policies for the same risk, they cannot claim the full loss from each. Instead, the insurers share the loss proportionately so the insured does not profit.

questions.stem: The cumulative satisfaction that a consumer derives from the consumption of successive units of a good is;
explanation_steps: **Total Utility** is the overall level of satisfaction or happiness a consumer gains from consuming a specific quantity of a good or service. It is the sum of marginal utilities.

questions.stem: Which of the following posting process come last?

options.A: record the date of the transaction in the general ledger account
options.B: record the general journal reference and page number in the posting reference column
options.C: locate in the general ledger the account debited in the journal entry
options.D: determine the balance in the account
options.E: enter the account number of the ledger account in the posting reference column of the journal

explanation_steps: The final step in the posting process is to write the ledger account number back into the 'Post Ref' column of the journal to indicate that the entry has been successfully posted.

questions.stem: When a company make entry on the debit side it:
explanation_steps:
According to the rules of double-entry bookkeeping:
- A **Debit** increases Assets and Expenses.
- A **Debit** decreases Liabilities, Equity, and Revenue.

questions.stem: All of the following are advantages of subsidiary ledger, **except**

options.A: up to date information on specific account
options.B: free the general ledger of excessive details
options.C: helps locate errors in individual account
options.D: show transactions affecting one customer or creditor in a single account

explanation_steps: All the options (A, B, C, and D) are actual advantages of using subsidiary ledgers. They provide detail, keep the general ledger clean, and help in error detection.

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is true?

options.A: Gross investment is solely determined by the rate of interest,
options.B: Gross investment is positively related to the rate of interest,
options.C: Gross investment is negatively related to the consumption,
options.D: Gross investment is negatively related to the rate of interest,

explanation_steps: Investment is **negatively related** to the rate of interest. When interest rates rise, the cost of borrowing increases, making investments more expensive and less attractive, leading to a decrease in gross investment.

questions.stem: MR. Robel earns 14 Nakfa per hour for a 40 hour week and works overtime after 10pm. If Robel works 45 hours in a week, his gross pay is;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Regular Pay.**
$$ 40 \text{ hours} \times 14 \text{ Nakfa/hr} = 560 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 2: Calculate Overtime Pay.**
Overtime hours = $$ 45 - 40 = 5 \text{ hours} $$.
Standard overtime rate is usually 1.5 times the regular rate.
$$ 14 \times 1.5 = 21 \text{ Nakfa/hr} $$
$$ 5 \text{ hours} \times 21 \text{ Nakfa/hr} = 105 \text{ Nakfa} $$

**Step 3: Calculate Total Gross Pay.**
$$ 560 + 105 = 665 \text{ Nakfa} $$

questions.stem:

questions.stem: The third stage in development of money is _______.
explanation_steps:
The historical stages of money are generally: 
1. **Commodity Money** (salt, cattle)
2. **Metallic Money** (gold, silver coins)
3. **Paper Money**
4. **Credit/Bank Money** (cheques, cards).

questions.stem: High degree of interdependence is the main feature of ______________ market.
explanation_steps: In an **Oligopoly**, there are only a few large sellers. Because they are few, the actions of one firm (like changing prices) significantly affect the others, leading to high interdependence.

questions.stem: Which of the following are **not** properties of indifference curve?

options.A: indifference curve bow inward toward the origin

explanation_steps: Indifference curves represent combinations of goods that provide the same utility. They must have **negative slopes** (downward sloping) because to get more of one good, the consumer must give up some of the other to keep utility constant.

questions.stem: Warsay Yikealo have a beginning cash balance on April 30, 2020 Nakfa $$ 10,000 $$ and amount received during the month Nakfa $$ 5,000 $$ and paid Nakfa $$ 15,000 $$. What will be the amount of cash on hand?
explanation_steps:

$$ \text{Ending Balance} = 10,000 + 5,000 - 15,000 = 0 $$

questions.stem: Posting:

options.B: Transfers ledger transactions to the journal.
options.C: An optional step in the recording process.
options.D: Transfers journal entries into the ledger account.

explanation_steps: **Posting** is the process of transferring information (debits and credits) from the journal (the book of original entry) to the ledger (the book of accounts).

questions.stem: Sales return and allowance for merchandise sold on account is recorded in
explanation_steps: Special journals are for high-volume, repetitive transactions. While credit sales go to the Sales Journal, a return of merchandise sold on account is typically recorded in the General Journal because it doesn't fit the specific criteria of the other special journals.

questions.stem: Most nations of the world are,
explanation_steps: In the modern era of globalization, almost all countries engage in international trade (exports and imports), making them **Open Economies**.

questions.stem: A certificate consists the name of each employee, accumulates the regular and overtime working hours is called__________.
explanation_steps: A **Time Card** (or time sheet) is the document used to record the specific hours an employee starts and finishes work, including regular and overtime hours.

questions.stem: The main duty of an insurance company is;
explanation_steps: The primary function of insurance is to **compensate** (indemnify) the policyholder for a specific loss or damage in exchange for payment of a premium.

questions.stem: All of the following are factors that shift demand curve **except**,
explanation_steps: A change in the **price of the product itself** causes a movement *along* the demand curve (change in quantity demanded), not a *shift* of the entire curve.

questions.stem: All of the following are characteristics of oligopoly market **except**,

options.B: They produce homogenous or heterogeneous products
options.C: There is few degree of competition among sellers

explanation_steps: In an **Oligopoly**, competition is actually very intense, though it is often non-price competition (advertising, branding). Firms are highly interdependent, meaning the actions of one firm significantly affect others.

questions.stem: Which of the following errors cannot be detected by preparing a trial balance?

options.B: record only one portion of a transaction

options.D: incorrectly recording debits as credit or credits as debit

questions.stem: The purchase of supplies on account should result in:
